Emotions in Drawdowns and Rallies
The Maths of a Fall
A 50% fall needs a 100% rise to recover; an 80% fall needs 400%.
Iran’s market has seen large, multi-year falls from a peak (such as after the 1399 peak). Assume from the start that you will live through a 40 to 50 percent fall.
Rise needed to recover = 1 ÷ (1 − fall) − 1
In a Fall, in a Rally
In a fall, first ask: “Has sustainable profit changed, or only the price?” If only the price, the fall may be an opportunity; carry out the step-by-step buying you wrote in advance.
In a rally: recalculate each stock’s payback; when everyone says “this time is different”, go back to your target weights.
The 48-hour rule: no unplanned buy or sell is carried out sooner than 48 hours after the decision.

Position Size and the Risk of Ruin
Risk of Ruin
The chance that a loss gets so big you can’t continue. Three sources in Iran:
Leverage (broker credit, loans for the market): with price limits and sell queues you may not be able to get out. FIS doesn’t use leverage.
Concentration: one stock or industry at 50% of the portfolio.
The wrong money: money you need in the next 1 to 2 years.
A Position Size Example
Stock capital 1 billion tomans and a 10% cap → the cap per company is 100 million tomans.
If the worst reasonable scenario is a 60% fall, the loss to the whole portfolio is 6%; bearable.
For riskier companies (the base market, thin margins), halve the cap.
If you’re scared, the amount isn’t your size. Cut it down to the point where it no longer matters to you

Financial Intelligence and the Goldun Law
Financial Intelligence
Financial intelligence is a problem-solving skill, not the size of your income.
Its most important skill is prioritising: first work out which is your main problem: earning more, or cutting costs?
Investing in yourself (skills and financial logic) is the first investment. The tools he considers necessary are simple: a calculator, a laptop and logic.
Financial intelligence, or financial IQ, is a person’s ability to solve their own and others’ financial problems.
Blog, “What is financial intelligence?”, Azar 1398
The Goldun Law
His book and course on living in harmony with the laws of nature (the book “The Goldun Law: 20 golden laws of nature that will transform your life”, Bahar-e Sabz publishing). The first three laws:
1. No comparing: your measure of progress is yesterday’s you, not other people.
2. Find your soil: with the flowerpot metaphor, find the environment and work in which you grow.
3. Know your needs: needs are found through self-knowledge (Maslow’s pyramid, from basic needs to self-actualisation), and meeting them takes balance.
The link with investing: a money goal that comes from your real need is lasting; a goal that comes from comparison pulls you into too much risk.

Fear of Action, and Time
A story he tells in his channel: a farmer who never sows for fear of rain and pests. Someone who does nothing out of fear loses the most.
The antidote to fear isn’t recklessness, it’s a plan: start small, a paper portfolio, a cap per stock, an emergency fund.
The 15-year plan he suggests for children’s financial independence rests on one principle: time is the most important variable in compounding. But always measure the real return (after inflation).

Money, Real Wealth and Investing in Yourself
Is Knowledge Better, or Wealth?
The name of one of his talks. Its answer isn’t simple, but it has two clear conclusions:
Wealth without knowledge is likely to be lost.
Success and wealth come from creating value at scale, meaning meeting the needs of more people, and their higher aim is spiritual wealth.

He also raises these questions: work you love or work that makes money? Is there a shortcut to getting rich? Is saving and cutting spending alone enough? Write your own answers in your journal and see his in the same video.
